result.title: Keyframes First, Motion Second: Revisiting Compressed-Domain Video Captioning under Limited Supervision
result.summary: Compressed-domain video captioners such as CoCap read the H.264 bitstream directly: a pretrained encoder reads the keyframes (I-frames), while motion and residual encoders, trained from scratch, turn the codec's motion vectors and residuals into action tokens. This motion branch costs decoding time and supervision, both scarce on edge devices. We ask when it pays off under limited supervision. In a controlled study on 2,500 VATEX training clips, we fix a frozen SigLIP 2 keyframe encoder, a GPT-2 caption decoder and the training schedule, vary only the visual tokens the decoder receives (34 configurations), and report held-out test CIDEr with paired bootstrap intervals and three seeds. Motion encoders trained from scratch bring no measurable benefit: CoCap-style action tokens change CIDEr by -0.55 (95% CI [-2.3, +1.2]), and six other uses of motion do not help. Warm-started from a model trained on 48x the caption samples, they add +1.3 CIDEr on average, though not significantly across seeds, and only while the keyframe tokens stay frozen. Reading the keyframes better matters more: fine-tuning SigLIP 2's own attention-pooling head adds 5.4 CIDEr, and one to eight such tokens beat the 16 CoCap-style tokens on every seed while decoding only I-frames (7.3 ms instead of 44-114 ms per clip). The same holds on MSVD's full split in CoCap's own video encoding, where the readout leads by 14.2 CIDEr and action tokens bring no reliable gain, also with clean single-reference motion vectors. Under limited supervision, keyframes come first and motion second.

AI.brief_summary: 在压缩域视频描述任务上做受控消融：固定冻结的 SigLIP 2 关键帧编码器、GPT-2 解码器与训练日程，仅改变解码器收到的视觉 token（34 种配置），比较运动/残差分支与不同关键帧读出方式的 CIDEr 与解码延迟。
AI.relevance_reason: 其关于视觉 token 数量、读出方式与延迟的受控比较，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与「看哪里、看多少」的成本收益权衡提供参照，但任务为视频描述、不涉及推理状态或停止决策，可迁移性需核查。
